thread:
elena: Heads up — after the kernel-routing tweak yesterday, we're seeing a 15–30ms p50 regression for requests with high prefix/KV cache hit rates. Stack: rye-rt v2.4 + kernel-selector v1.7. Repro steps attached. Anyone else seeing this?

jay: I noticed a small shift on canary too. p95 looks fine but p50 moved up. Was kernel selector updated to prefer "fastpath_delta" for hit-heavy flows?

omar: attaching sampled trace from perf-bot: https://perf.local/traces/2376543210 — key lines from the runtime log: 
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:35Z] kernel=fastpath_delta chosen_score=0.72 kv_cache_hit=true microbatch=1 tokens=24 dispatch_latency_ms=3.8
[2026-03-18T09:12:35Z] packer=prefix-aware pack_sz=1 packed_with_hits=3 queue_wait_ms=1.2
[2026-03-18T09:12:35Z] kernel=throughput_fused chosen_score=0.65 kv_cache_hit=false microbatch=4 tokens=128 dispatch_latency_ms=2.1
```
Logs show we ended up with many 1-microbatch kernels chosen for hit-only traffic. Dispatch latency per-request rose.

maria: profiler snapshot (sampled): 
```
CPU profiles: scheduler: 28% (pack/unpack), kernel-selector: 9%, queue-manager: 12%
GPU kernels: fastpath_delta small_batch_launch_overhead=0.9ms kernel_exec=0.5ms
throughput_fused launch_overhead=0.2ms kernel_exec=3.2ms (amortized over bigger microbatches)
```
So fastpath_delta has lower per-token exec but higher launch overhead relative to its tiny compute — bad when microbatch=1 dominates.

tim: quick intuition — when KV cache hits are high, the packer often emits very short token budgets (common prefix saved), so requests look "cheap" and kernel-selector favors the low-latency kernel. But that increases per-request launch overhead because we lose batching efficiency. Net effect p50 up.

elena: yeah. two levers: (A) make packer prefer mixing in non-hit requests to increase microbatch sizes; (B) make kernel-selector consider the expected downstream microbatch_size and penalize fastpath_delta for small throughput.

jay: propose A/B test: variant A toggle packer:mix_ratio=0.10 (allow up to 10% non-hit filler) vs variant B kernel-selector: min_microbatch_for_fastpath=4. Run for 2 hours during low traffic. Metrics: p50_token_latency, tokens/sec/GPU, cache_hit_rate, pack_sz distribution.

omar: I'll instrument the packer to emit a small histogram: `pack_sz_histogram=[1:3245,2:1120,3:420,4+:210]` and add `expected_kernel_choice` sampling into traces. Should help correlate kernel choice -> latency.

perf-bot: trace sample created: https://perf.local/traces/2376543210/summary — sampled 200 requests, 76% kv_cache_hit, median_pack_sz=1, mean_dispatch_latency_ms=3.6, p50_token_latency_delta=18ms (vs baseline).

maria: small experiment idea: if we bias packer to cap token_budget_floor=32 tokens for hit-only requests (i.e., artificially enlarge tiny budgets to allow better batch packing), do we risk quality/regressions? We need to run eval on a small prompt set.

elena: good point — we must avoid changing model quality. For the quick perf experiment, keep behavior isolated to interior canary traffic and add a quality smoke eval for the prompt set. If quality looks fine, we can iterate.

jay: I'll stand up the A/B, add the pack_sz histogram and kernel_choice tags, and push run config. ETA ~ 90m. @omar can you add the sampled-trace link into the dashboard so SLO alerts can watch p50 drift?

omar: on it. Will also add a tiny dashboard card that shows fraction of requests where `kernel=fastpath_delta AND microbatch=1`.

elena: thanks — let's reconvene in #eng-runtime in ~2.5h with results. If we see the expected smoothing benefit from mixing filler requests or raising the min_microbatch threshold, we can pick the safer change (likely kernel-selector tweak) and roll it out. :thumbsup:

jay: ack, will post results.

maria: noted — I'll run the prompt-set quality checks once we have trace-level picks.

perf-bot: job perf-sample/2376543210 completed (200 samples). Artifacts uploaded to s3://perf-artifacts/2376543210/ — includes flamegraphs, packer_hist.csv, kernel_decisions.json

elena: perfect. thanks everyone. If anything spikes, escalate here.
